summary: This note is a short encyclopedia-style entry on the Toyota Corona, a car Toyota manufactured from 1957 to 2002. It notes that the Nissan Bluebird was its traditional competitor and explains that the name "corona" is Latin for "crown", referring to Toyota's earlier Crown model. The note also states that the Corona was sold through Toyopet Store dealerships in Japan, while the larger Crown was sold only at Toyota Store locations.
one_line: The Toyota Corona is a Japanese automobile made by Toyota from 1957 to 2002, named after the Latin word for crown.
key_facts: The Toyota Corona is an automobile manufactured by the Japanese automaker Toyota between 1957 and 2002.
Traditionally, the Toyota Corona's competitor from Nissan was the Nissan Bluebird.
The name Corona refers to an earlier Toyota vehicle called the Toyota Crown.
The Toyota Corona was exclusive to "Toyopet Store" dealership channels in Japan.
The larger Toyota Crown was available only at "Toyota Store" locations.
The Toyota Corona was produced for 45 years, from 1957 to 2002.
